selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: In the passage, what happens among people who say something is true?
questions.answer: Their statements point to one shared result, so they support one another.

questions.question: Why is negation described as many instead of one?
questions.answer: Because each person denies based on his own separate way of seeing things.

questions.question: Why can denials not easily join together into one strong case?
questions.answer: Because each denial comes from a separate personal judgment.

questions.question: What should Muslims understand about the apparent strength of unbelievers?
questions.answer: Their seeming strength in numbers has no real weight against truth.

questions.question: What should not be weakened by spreading hesitation?
questions.answer: A believer’s firm iman should not be weakened.

questions.question: What outside influence is said to have caused doubts in some people?
questions.answer: Ideas of some European philosophers caused those doubts.

questions.question: How is death described for a person who denies faith?
questions.answer: It is shown as total ending instead of a leaving from this world.

questions.question: What picture does the passage give of the grave for someone without faith?
questions.answer: It appears like an open doorway to destruction and sadness.

questions.question: Why does the grave become frightening for the denier?
questions.answer: Because he thinks it leads only to annihilation.

questions.question: What is the best summary of the last line of the passage?
questions.answer: Faith is a tremendous blessing and the heart of truly living.

questions.question: In this passage, which is united into one result: affirmation or negation?
questions.answer: Affirmation is united into one result.

questions.question: What relationship does the passage show between one denial and another denial?
questions.answer: They do not truly strengthen each other.

questions.question: Why does the passage say separate denials cannot all hold each other up?
questions.answer: Because they do not rest on one common, positive truth.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the seeming majority of deniers?
questions.answer: It says their majority does not matter in proving truth.

questions.question: What must be guarded carefully in a believer?
questions.answer: His certainty in faith must be guarded.

questions.question: What happened to those misled people when doubt entered their hearts?
questions.answer: Their certainty was broken, and they lost the happiness that would have lasted forever.

questions.question: How is death wrongly presented by deniers?
questions.answer: They see it as endless non-existence.

questions.question: How do deniers interpret the arrival of death?
questions.answer: They take it as the end of a person forever.

questions.question: What false meaning is put in its place?
questions.answer: It is treated as never existing again.

questions.question: How does that fear affect the denier’s life?
questions.answer: It makes life bitter and full of grief.

questions.question: What relationship does the passage show between one affirmation and another affirmation?
questions.answer: They back each other up.

questions.question: How does personal opinion affect denial?
questions.answer: It makes each denial separate because it depends on the individual person.

questions.question: What does this teach about counting how many people reject belief?
questions.answer: Numbers alone do not decide what is true.

questions.question: What conclusion does the passage make about many unbelievers standing against belief?
questions.answer: Their large number still does not give their denial real importance.
